exposure: First trimester levels of placental growth factor (PlGF)
cohort: The study included 180 singleton pregnant females without multiple/molar pregnancies, smoking, or chronic hypertension, screened in a tertiary center of North India.
finding: Low first-trimester PlGF levels were significantly associated with adverse maternal outcomes (including maternal death, eclampsia, HELLP, pulmonary edema, abruption, postpartum hemorrhage, cesarean section, preeclampsia) and composite fetal adverse outcomes (including intrauterine death, SGA, respiratory distress syndrome, necrotizing enterocolitis, intraventricular hemorrhage, NICU admission).
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as an adverse maternal outcome significantly associated with low PlGF levels.
